subject: Fitting a Maximum Entropy Distribution from Kernel in Stan

messages.author: 06167d8d45a67c62
messages.subject: Fitting a Maximum Entropy Distribution from Kernel in Stan
parts:
Hello everyone, 

I have data for which I would like to fit a custom distribution and report the posteriors for the distribution parameters. The form of the distribution is derived through a maximum entropy problem for data x \in Reals with five parameters (see attached). I'm wondering if it's possible to estimate the posteriors for the model parameters from the kernel of the maxent distribution alone, given the intractability of solving the normalizing integral.

So far, I have been estimating the model parameters in Mathematica by solving the maximum entropy program, which estimates a frequency distribution \hat{f}[x], and then finding the parameters that minimize the Kullback-Leibler distance between the estimated frequencies \hat{f}[x] and observed frequencies f[x]. However, I would like to report full posteriors for the model parameters. 

The parameter values that minimize the KL divergence (and give very good fits) for the attached data are: 

{\[Mu] -> 2.82139, \[Gamma] -> -6.98368, \[Delta] -> 0.0611006, T -> 0.0597599, \[Delta]bar -> -0.00993992, \[Beta] -> 17.9291}

I thought it might be possible to use the following model in Stan:

model {
  for (n in 1:N)
  target += -inv_logit((x[n]-mu)/T)*log_inv_logit((x[n]-mu)/T)-inv_logit(-(x[n]-mu)/T)*log_inv_logit(-(x[n]-mu)/T)-gamma*x[n]-inv_logit((x[n]-mu)/T)*beta*(x[n]-delta);
} 

But without the partition function I'm not sure this is possible. Any suggestions would be greatly appreciated. Thanks in advance.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Fitting a Maximum Entropy Distribution from Kernel in Stan
parts:
Given that your partition function (normalizing term)
depends on the parameters, you need it as part of the log
density if you want to compute a posterior.

I don't know how to get around that or if there's
a way to formulate your model as a likelihood and prior
that Stan can compute.

In general, computing partition functions itself requires
MCMC integration. Stan does that under the hood for variational
inference, which also involves minimizing a KL divergence.

- Bob
